tiktok.author: khanjicyber
tiktok.body:
The FBI would like a word with anyone using a pirated cable box. Over 10 million cheap Android streaming boxes were sold with malware already inside them, installed at the factory in China. The moment they were plugged in, they joined a criminal network that rents out your home internet connection for as little as 20 cents. Attacks on banks, account takeovers, and some of the biggest DDoS attacks ever recorded were routed through people’s living rooms. In November one of these networks fired off 1.7 billion attack commands in three days and briefly out-ranked Google in global traffic. I don’t know how useful a full list of affected models would be, but at a high level please check if you’re running a (X96, T95, TV98, MXQ, SuperBox as they’re the main ones. Want the full story? Darknet Diaries Ep 172 “SuperBox” is a brilliant deep dive on the researcher who helped uncover it. Link in bio. Sources: FBI Public Service Announcement I-060525-PSA (June 2025), Google v Does lawsuit (July 2025), HUMAN Security Satori BadBox 2.0 report, Krebs on Security, The Hacker News, Rescana, EFF. Note: not every unit of a listed model is infected, but infections are confirmed within these model lines. If you own one, treat it as compromised.
If you use any of these pirated free cable boxes, the FBI would like to have a chat with you. And it's not because of piracy, it's because you've been learning hackers your IP address to carry out some of the biggest cyber attacks in history. And it's all happening without you realising. And I'm a cyber security expert. Let me show you exactly how they did it. So hackers have actually had a foothold inside your home Wi-Fi where they could see unencrypted sites you visited, uh, reach other devices in your house and use your internet connection to run some of the biggest cyber attacks in history. And you know the box I'm talking about, you know the, the $200 one that your uncle gives you where has every channel, you know, Netflix for free, every movie, but nobody gives you thousands of dollars of content for free. So if you're not the customer, remember, you're the product. So over 10 million of these were sold on Aliexpress and Tmall with malware already inside them installed at the factory. So before you even open the box, it's working for someone else. And the moment you plug it in, it quietly joins a criminal network. And all of this information is from an FBI investigation and Google's also suing the people behind it. So once it's plugged into your home network, uh, it joins what's called like a residential proxy service. And in plain English, it just kind of helps The criminals route their traffic through your home IP address so the attack looks like it came from your house and not their service so what's your home connection worth on the black market? Some researchers have said that the going rate is about 20 cents a gigabyte buyers basically use it for what the FBI calls confidential stuffing and which means using your IP to break into other people's accounts with stolen passwords and ad fraud and just even doing cyber attacks at scale and late last year one of these networks uh mostly from these boxes actually fired out over a billion attack commands in just three days and the command server for a moment was actually ranking above Google in global traffic so boxes sitting inside your house and that's even after the German authorities actually shut down the first major network however it was back online within a few weeks with a few hundred thousand devices there is an official list of the exact box models that the FBI and Google identified and some of these are just still being sold on Amazon and Aliexpress and in me right now so if you're interested in knowing which box check out the comments and if you found this story interesting Darknet Diaries actually did an amazing episode on it uh which I've put the link uh in my bio and if you want to stay safe online give this a follow because I'm gonna continue tracking...
